paper_metadata.title: Quantification of Solid Solution Strengthening and Internal Stresses through Creep Testing of Ni-Containing Single Crystals at 980 °C

evidence.quote: Single crystal Ni-based superalloys used as blade material in the hottest section of stationary gas turbines and aero-engines must withstand high static and dynamic stresses at high temperatures in an oxidizing atmosphere.
pure Ni, the equiatomic alloys CoCrNi and CrMnFeCoNi (Cantor alloy)
Seven different Ni-containing single-crystalline alloys have been creep tested.
Table 1 lists the composition of the alloys cast and creep tested in at.%. The Ni-content varies from 20 to 100 at.%.
(A) Pure Ni (single-phase fcc) with 99.9 at.% technical purity and configurational entropy equal to zero. No heat treatment was carried out.
(B) Equiatomic alloys with single-phase fcc microstructure: CrCoNi with 33.3 at.% for each element and the so-called Cantor alloy (CrMnFeCoNi with 20 at.% each) [26].
